parsedVerdict.reasoning: The file is declared application-layer, and *.dto.ts files map to application in the layer model. Two classes live in it. CancelOrderDto is the use case's input shape (orderId plus reason), which fits the application role. CancelOrderBodyDto is different: its own doc comment calls it "The transport contract for POST /orders/:id/cancel". It is the HTTP request body for one route, checked with class-validator @IsString() decorators, so that validation is tied to a framework at the request boundary. The comment on CancelOrderDto ("once the controller has merged in the path id") also builds controller and route-parameter details into the use case's input. Request body shape and validation for a specific HTTP endpoint are transport/presentation work, which is infrastructure kind (src/orders/presentation/orders.controller.ts is where that belongs). This is a judgement call: many NestJS projects put validation decorators on application DTOs. Here, though, the file names itself as the transport contract, which points to a misplaced transport responsibility.
